questions.text:
Consider the following C functions.

The return value of fun2(5) is ______
questions.solution:
Both functions keep a static i that is never reset. fun1(n) adds n to its own i and returns it.
fun2(5) adds fun1(5), fun1(4), [latex]\ldots[/latex], fun1(1) to fun2's i:
- fun1(5) = 5, fun1(4) = 9, fun1(3) = 12, fun1(2) = 14, fun1(1) = 15

fun2's i = 5 + 9 + 12 + 14 + 15 = 55

Answer: 55

questions.text: Consider the array representation of a binary min-heap containing 1023 elements. The minimum number of comparisons required to find the maximum in the heap is ___________.
questions.solution:
In a min-heap the maximum is always at a leaf. With 1023 nodes there are [latex]\lceil1023/2\rceil=512[/latex] leaves.

Finding the maximum of 512 elements needs 512 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 511 comparisons.

Answer: 511

questions.text:
Consider the following C functions.

The value returned by pp(3,4) is _____
questions.solution:
tob(b, arr) stores the binary digits of b (LSB first) and returns their count. b = 4 = 100[latex]{}_2[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] arr = [0, 0, 1], len = 3.

pp computes [latex]a^b[/latex] by repeated squaring: ex goes 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 81, and tot is multiplied only where the bit is 1 (the third bit) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] tot = 81.

[latex]3^4=81[/latex]

Answer: 81

questions.text: Consider a graph [latex]G=(V,E)[/latex], where [latex]V=\{v_1,v_2,...,v_{100}\}[/latex], [latex]E=\{(v_i,v_j)|1\leq i \lt j\leq 100\}[/latex], and weight of the edge [latex](v_i,v_j)\; is \; |i-j|[/latex]. The weight of minimum spanning tree of G is _________
questions.solution:
Edge weight is |i [latex]-[/latex] j| [latex]\ge1[/latex], and weight 1 is possible only between consecutive vertices. The 99 edges [latex](v_i,v_{i+1})[/latex] form a spanning tree (a path) of weight 1 each.

Any spanning tree has 99 edges of weight at least 1, so this is minimum: 99.

Answer: 99

questions.text:
Consider the following set of processes, assumed to have arrived at time 0. Consider the CPU scheduling algorithms Shortest Job First (SJF) and Round Robin (RR). For RR, assume that the processes are scheduled in the order [latex]P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4[/latex].

If the time quantum for RR is 4 ms, then the absolute value of the difference between the average turnaround times (in ms) of SJF and RR (round off to 2 decimal places is_______
questions.solution:
SJF (P3 2, P4 4, P2 7, P1 8): completion 2, 6, 13, 21 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average TAT = 42 / 4 = 10.5

RR, q = 4: P1 0-4, P2 4-8, P3 8-10 (done), P4 10-14 (done), P1 14-18 (done), P2 18-21 (done)
TAT: P1 18, P2 21, P3 10, P4 14 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average = 63 / 4 = 15.75

|15.75 [latex]-[/latex] 10.5| = 5.25

Answer: 5.25
